technical_and_design_decisions: Domain and application lifecycle management (U1, U2) will be implemented by extending the existing Mule DeploymentService rather than introducing a new API, to preserve backward compatibility with existing deployments.
Domain redeploy (U1) will internally perform an undeploy of the domain and all child apps followed by a deploy, so that an explicit cascade semantic can be reused for hot updates.

Application property override (U2) will be implemented as a layered property resolver that injects override values after the app bundle's own properties are loaded, so app defaults can still be overridden cleanly.
AMQP transport schema (U4) will be delivered as an XSD file referenced by the AMQP namespace, enabling IDE auto-completion and validation in Mule XML configurations.
Base project skeleton (U5) will be provided as a Maven archetype so it can be reused across teams and versioned with the framework.
Centralized transport configuration (U6) will leverage Mule's existing 'global element' / reusable definitions mechanism (template-style definitions referenced by name).
Continuous AMQP consumption (U7) will be implemented as an inbound endpoint / message source that translates each AMQP message into a MuleEvent and dispatches it to the configured flow.
Instant/on-demand AMQP consumption (U8) will be implemented as an outbound message processor ('amqp:consume') that can be invoked at any point of a flow to fetch a message on demand.

Specs review capability (U3) will be implemented as a public, versioned set of Markdown/AsciiDoc specs in a public Git repository with a contribution guide and review process; no custom tooling will be built.
A single integrated codebase is assumed, using Java 8, Maven, JUnit/Mockito for unit testing, and Mule's functional test framework for integration testing.
assumptions: The base Mule ESB framework, the AMQP transport, and the basic DeploymentService already exist; these user stories represent extensions and refinements, not green-field development.
A single mid-to-senior developer performs all the work, with no team coordination overhead.
1 workday equals 8 hours of focused development effort.
A public Git repository, contribution guide, and review process already exist or require only minimal setup for the specs review feature (U3).
IDE auto-completion is satisfied by shipping a well-formed XSD with proper documentation annotations; no plugin work is required.
Test infrastructure (CI, Maven test runners, AMQP test broker such as RabbitMQ) is already available.
Requirements are stable and no rework beyond minor adjustments is required.
Documentation is concise and high-level, targeting experienced Mule users.

activities.activity_description: Design the API extensions to DeploymentService for deploying, undeploying, and redeploying domains, including return types, exceptions, and cascade semantics for child applications.
Implement the deploy method that registers a domain bundle, starts its shared resources, and makes it available for hosted applications.
Implement the undeploy method that gracefully stops and removes a domain, also stopping and undeploying all applications hosted by it.
Implement the redeploy method that re-uses the undeploy/deploy pipeline to refresh the domain bundle and propagate the update to all child applications.
Write unit tests and functional/integration tests covering deploy, undeploy, redeploy, error cases, and the cascade lifecycle of hosted apps.
Design how DeploymentService accepts external property values and how they are merged with the app bundle's own properties at deployment time.

activities.activity_name: Implement app deploy with property overrides
activities.activity_description: Extend the application deploy entry point to accept override properties, integrate them into the property resolver chain, and persist them for the app's lifetime.

activities.activity_name: Test app deploy with property overrides
activities.activity_description: Write unit and functional tests verifying that override properties take precedence over bundle properties and that missing keys behave as expected.
Create or configure a public Git repository, contribution guide, review checklist, and tagging/versioning conventions for specs.
Author the initial set of specifications (e.g., AMQP transport, deployment model) as Markdown/AsciiDoc documents ready for community review and feedback.
Design the XSD schema for the AMQP transport namespace, covering connector, endpoint, and message-receiver elements with required/optional attributes and documentation.
Register the XSD with the AMQP namespace, wire it into the Mule schema set, and ensure XML parsing uses it for validation of AMQP configurations.

activities.activity_name: Document IDE usage of the schema
activities.activity_description: Document how IDEs (Eclipse, IntelliJ) automatically pick up the schema via the namespace declaration, including a sample XML header.
Design the directory layout, placeholder files, and configuration of the Maven archetype that will serve as the base Mule project skeleton.
Implement the Maven archetype (pom, mule-config.xml, README, sample flows with stable placeholders for endpoints, connectors, and transactions) and publish/install it.
Design the pattern for declaring common transport attributes once and referencing them from multiple flows (e.g., via Mule's template/global definition mechanism).
Implement the XML/runtime support so that a single transport configuration element can be referenced by name from any flow in the application.

activities.activity_name: Test and document centralized transport config
activities.activity_description: Write tests verifying that overriding or extending a shared transport config behaves correctly, and document the pattern in user docs.
Implement the inbound message source that continuously listens on an AMQP queue, creates a MuleEvent for each message, and dispatches it to the configured flow.

activities.activity_name: Integrate continuous consumer with Mule event flow
activities.activity_description: Wire the continuous consumer into the Mule lifecycle (start/stop, exception handling, transactions) and ensure it works with the rest of the event pipeline.
Write functional tests with a real or embedded broker verifying that messages are consumed, converted to MuleEvents, and routed to the target flow.
Implement the on-demand message processor that pulls a single message from an AMQP queue when invoked at any point in a flow.
Integrate the instant consumer as an outbound message processor usable inside any flow, including handling of empty queues and timeouts.
Write functional tests verifying that the on-demand consumer correctly retrieves messages, handles empty queues, and propagates the result downstream.
Write the user documentation covering domain management, property overrides, AMQP transport schema, project skeleton, and both consumption modes.
Run a full end-to-end test pass across all the new features in a representative Mule runtime, including domain redeploy with running apps, property overrides, and AMQP flows.
